notes: All FY2023-FY2025 income statement and D&A figures used here come from Wynn’s FY2025 Form 10-K consolidated segment reconciliation tables (amounts were reported in thousands and converted to full USD). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Capex totals (FY2023-FY2025) come from the FY2025 Form 10-K 'Capital expenditures' note (converted from thousands to full USD). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

NWC is a model proxy computed from year-end balance-sheet current items: (Current assets − cash & cash equivalents − short-term investments − restricted cash within current assets) − (Current liabilities − current portion of long-term debt). This proxy is negative for all three years, driven largely by customer deposits/payables versus receivables/inventories. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Tax rate assumption (0.21) is normalized because GAAP income tax expense/benefit and valuation allowance movements can distort the effective rate in individual years. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492225000039/wynn-20241231.htm))

WACC and terminal exit multiple are base-case modeling assumptions (not explicitly disclosed as a single published input). They should be treated as placeholders for your desk’s standard capital structure and beta/market-implied inputs.

catalysts: Wynn Al Marjan Island opening and initial operating ramp (expected 2027), with further contribution from adjacent Janu Al Marjan (late 2028). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Macau operating momentum (room revenue and premium trends) flowing through to consolidated operating income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
Execution of the disclosed 2026-2027 capex cycle without cost overruns or regulatory delays. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Integrated casino resort operator with segments focused on Macau (Wynn Palace, Wynn Macau) and the U.S. (Las Vegas operations and Encore Boston Harbor). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Historical financials show a step-up in operating income from 2023 to 2024, with 2025 remaining strong but broadly stable in scale. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Major development catalyst: Wynn Al Marjan Island expected to open in 2027 (with adjacent Janu Al Marjan expected late 2028). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 operating revenues were $7,137,924,000 and operating income (EBIT) was $1,118,384,000. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
FY2025 depreciation and amortization were $620,633,000 and capital expenditures were $660,433,000. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Capex outlook in filings: estimated Macau project capital expenditures of $400,000,000-$450,000,000 in 2026 and $425,000,000-$475,000,000 in 2027 (plus Macau maintenance capex $70,000,000-$80,000,000 in 2026). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Recent performance discussion highlights sensitivity of operating results to Macau room revenue trends. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth resumes to a modest mid-single-digit profile (post-2025 stabilization), consistent with property-level maturity and new opening ramp timing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin is anchored to the realized 2023-2025 range (roughly mid-teens), with only gradual progression in the outyears rather than a step-change. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Model D&A, capex intensity, and working-capital drag/tailwind are tied to FY2023-FY2025 history while reflecting a higher capex cycle beginning in 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Negative working capital (proxy-built from balance-sheet current items net of cash/investments and current debt) is treated as structurally recurring in the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Macau demand, competitive dynamics, and regulatory/concession risks that can pressure gaming economics and operating leverage. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Construction and project execution risk (timing/overrun) tied to Wynn Al Marjan and related expansion plans. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
Financing and interest-rate risk affecting free cash flow given the company’s sizable debt load. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

presentation.subtitle: WYNN DCF Input Package (Base/Bull/Bear)
valuation_summary: DCF base case uses a normalized tax rate (0.21), WACC of 0.085, and terminal growth of 0.025, with terminal value estimated via an exit EBITDA multiple. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))

Forecast drivers (EBIT margin, D&A%, capex%, NWC%) are calibrated to recent FY2023-FY2025 reported relationships and then carried forward with conservative improvements. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1174922/000117492226000013/wynn-20251231.htm))
Bull/bear cases are intentionally modest (±about 0.5pp on growth and ±about 0.3pp on EBIT margin, with small WACC/terminal changes) to support realistic sensitivity analysis.
